result.rationale: The trajectory shows a persistent pattern where the rescue team's health and position are eroded by environmental reactor-heat damage and hostile pirate pressure before the civilian rescue affordance becomes actionable. Engineer Imani drops from 100 to 16 health across turns 1-5, taking repeated scatter-blast hits from Raider Holt (29, 25) plus reactor-environment damage (10 each turn in reactor zones). Security Chen also takes reactor damage and Raider Holt scatter-blast (25). Meanwhile, the rescue objective (rescue-two-civilians) remains at 0/2 through all 6 turns. The key causal bottleneck is that the team is forced through/into reactor zones (reactor-entry, reactor-console) where reactor-instability hazard deals 10 damage/turn and where pirates (Hacker Nyx, Captain Veyra) are positioned, while the actual civilians (Kade at life-console, Sato at med-ward) are elsewhere. Medic Reyes successfully escorts Sato at turn 3 but then the escort route to rescue-airlock is blocked by Raider Holt (blockerActorIds: pirate-raider-holt) and Medic's move to junction-cover is contested (target_zone_capacity_lost). The spatial pressure (reactor hazard + pirate positioning + zone capacity) prevents the team from converting the available rescue affordance into progress. This is not a knowledge bottleneck (civilians are located and confirmed) nor a local-policy failure (the agent repeatedly attempts rescue-relevant actions), but rather hostile/environmental spatial pressure blocking the useful affordance.
